I just researched Senator Paul's taxation proposal and as a libertarian it's not something I really support (despite that I will vote for him in the upcoming election) and here's why:

  1. It's a progressive flat tax which is an example of an "unfair tax" for a couple of reasons.

    A. Part of it is a social engineering tax in which a family of four wouldn't have to pay income tax on the first 50,000 earned (I'm okay with that despite the fact i feel it incentivizes/ deincentivizes reproduction financially, and hence why I call it a "social engineering tax").

    B. According to CNN money (not expecting it to be reliable info...) in his tax structure, "Capital gains, dividends and interest would be tax free." This is a big no-no for me as the wealthiest members of our national community own the most stock and then therefore benefit disproportionately to the average worker/investor from this type of legislation.

    C. According to some of the things I have read it seems that he is also OK with offshore tax havens, which is also not a selling point. I could be mistaken, and if anybody has a source to refute that please let me know.

These are just a few problems I have with most progressive forms of taxation. EVEN FROM A CANDIDATE THAT I LIKE!

So honestly why not a True Flat Tax?

Wouldn't a True Flat Tax be optimal in it's simplicity and fairness?

My idea of the best True Flat Tax is one where everybody is taxed the same percent on all income earned. So dividends, capital gains, offshore income, increases in property value, etc. all get taxed the same percent. So, literally, ALL INCOME GENERATED. A person would get taxed at the same rate as a business/corporation as well. There would be no exemptions or tax breaks for families and it would eliminate the "social engineering" tax, but the biggest selling point is that if we saw this implemented across the board we could actually see a lower tax rate for the average citizen as everybody would have to pay their fair share of total income earned. This is because most corporations and wealthy businessmen/women are more equipped to exploit the tax system with offshore tax havens/buying legislation/etc.

In our current system the burden of a progressive tax seems to fall the heaviest on the lower classes in terms of percentage. Shouldn't we all share the tax burden of government equally?

Thoughts?
Why don't we ever hear any talk about a True Flat Tax? Everything is a "progressive" tax and nobody seems to argue for this opinion. So I will make the attempt.

The problem is that the cost of living isn't the same percentage for the rich and the poor.

So, once that necessary amount is removed, by having a flat percentage for all income, you actually end up with a higher tax for the poor. So in order to fix that, you usually end up with a progressive tax rate ( soon with exceptions for specific situations and needs to steer the economy )...

you actually end up with a higher tax for the poor.

Well as a true flat tax it wouldn't actually be higher for the poor as it's the same percent. So if I earned 100,000 dollars and the tax rate was 10% that would be 10,000 dollars and if I earned 15,000 it would be 1500.

So it's not a higher tax for the poor when it comes to the numbers.

The thing is though if you live below the poverty line and i take that percent when you already can't afford food or housing. Equal in numbers, higher in importance.

I wouldn't say I'm a proponent for a strict as heck true flat tax in which the state will kick down the doors of the poor to take their 100 bucks.

Maybe a True Flat Tax that is progressive in helping the poor and not the rich is more what I'm proposing here.
